thread:
lex_support: Ping team, customer 'NovaRetail' reporting rerank endpoint flakiness after upgrading SDK. Symptoms: sometimes all scores come back as strings from client ("0.5"), sometimes server responds 400 "scores must be numbers", and ranking order differs between Python and TS clients. Latency p95 for rerank also jumped.

maria_sdk: thanks. do we have raw request bodies and SDK versions? they said Python redwood-sdk==0.9.2 and TS @redwood/sdk 0.9.2.

lex_support: pasted examples (sanitized):
Python client sent:
```json
{"query":"best shipping option?","candidates":[{"id":"a","text":"Ground"},{"id":"b","text":"Air"}],"scores":["0.62","0.38"]}
```
TS client sent:
```json
{"query":"best shipping option?","candidates":[{"id":"a","text":"Ground"},{"id":"b","text":"Air"}],"scores":[0.62,0.38]}
```

zach_eng: server expects numeric arrays for scores. strings would hit validation and can cause 400. good catch. any idea why python serializes floats as strings?

maria_sdk: quick root cause: we added a safe-decimal serializer to normalize numeric types across inputs. a regression causes floats passed to rerank() to be wrapped into Decimal and then json encoder calls str() unconditionally. so numbers become JSON strings. reproducing locally now.

olivia_sre: operationally, when strings arrive we fall back to an expensive parse path that uses Decimal to re-parse each score for exactness; that path is slower (traces show ~300-500ms extra). also saw some cases where the gateway surfaced a 400 back to client and the SDK retried once due to a middleware bug in versions between 0.9.0-0.9.2 causing duplicate billing.

lex_support: customer also said ordering mismatch: TS request got expected ranking, Python request resulted in reversed order on server. could be because server treats string scores differently or because Python client strips candidate.metadata.\
maria_sdk: boolean: our Python client had an option that normalizes candidate objects and drops unknown keys by default. that might remove metadata tie-breakers. i'll test with metadata preserved.

zach_eng: i'll add a small server-side tolerance: accept numeric-strings by a fast float(...) cast path (pure C path) and log a tenant-level warning so we avoid the slow Decimal fallback. still want client fix ASAP.

maria_sdk: repro steps I'm running: create venv python3.10, pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.2, run this minimal script against staging endpoint:
```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key='REDACTED', base_url='https://staging.api.redwood.ai')
query = 'best shipping option?'
cands = [{'id':'a','text':'Ground'},{'id':'b','text':'Air'}]
scores = [0.62, 0.38]
print(c.rerank(query=query, candidates=cands, scores=scores))
```
run produces 400 with server message "invalid input: expected list<float> got list<string>" and staging trace id stg-4f12c. i can reproduce reliably.

maria_sdk: quick patch: special-case rerank payload builder to not call Decimal->str, push small PR to stop stringification of floats. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/509 (draft). will add unit test and changelog. aiming for 0.9.3 release.

zach_eng: on server i'm going to implement a fast acceptor: if type is string and it matches float regex, call fast_atof() and record a tenant warn metric. also add unit tests that verify ordering when scores are equal and metadata tie-breaks.

olivia_sre: looking at gateway logs for NovaRetail, there are 3 identical rerank POSTs within 2s for a single user action. gateway doesn't retry on 4xx; likely SDK middleware retried once due to misclassifying JSON parse error as transient. maria, can you confirm which SDK builds had that retry behavior?

maria_sdk: confirmed: a middleware change in 0.9.1 introduced a transient classification on JSONDecodeError for some responses; 0.9.2 included a partial fix but customers who upgraded during the window could have retried. i'll enumerate affected versions and include guidance for billing team.

lex_support: proposed next steps:
- maria: land hotfix to prevent float->str for rerank, release 0.9.3, and publish mitigation (curl example) and note versions affected. target: EOD.
- zach: add fast numeric-string acceptance and tenant warning, run canary on staging, then prod push if green.
- olivia: correlate duplicate requests to billing logs and flag potential duplicate charges for affected tenant, add a short blurb for billing team.
- lex_support: send NovaRetail a runbook and temporary workaround (raw HTTP payload or pin to TS SDK) and ETA.

maria_sdk: workaround curl for customer:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"best shipping option?","candidates":[{"id":"a","text":"Ground"},{"id":"b","text":"Air"}],"scores":[0.62,0.38]}'
```

lex_support: customer asked if we can do a temporary server-side fix so they don't need to change client code. zach - sounds like your warning + fast path will mitigate. can we also make the validation error message friendlier and include a hint about SDK versions?

zach_eng: yes, we'll change the 400 to include: "scores must be numeric array; Python SDK 0.9.2 may stringify floats—upgrade to 0.9.3 or send numeric scores." but we should be careful leaking internal SDK details; keep message actionable and generic.

olivia_sre: tickets: created INC-RED-4319 to track operational impact and billing audit.

maria_sdk: opened draft PR and running CI now. will post CI link and ETA here.

lex_support: great. I'll update NovaRetail with the workaround + ETA and offer to escalate billing review if they saw extra charges. marking P2. :white_check_mark:
